rows.evidence: Q1: Section 'Deficit irrigation in fruit trees and vines', Fig. 10 and Table 1 - the authors report their own multi-year peach experiment near Cordoba comparing RDI, SDI and full irrigation (stem water potential, yield, fruit volume), plus original model fits of Cordoba sunflower data (Figs 7-8).
rows.notes: The paper is predominantly a review of deficit irrigation, but it reports original data from a peach RDI/SDI experiment (Table 1, Fig. 10), so Q1 is answered yes with some doubt. The study contains no digital/app-based scheduling system, no weather-forecast or soil-moisture-driven decision tool; its own evidence concerns manually designed RDI vs SDI regimes in peach (RDI gave yield equal to full irrigation with two-thirds the water; SDI reduced yield 10%). The claim about digital systems combining crop stage, weather and soil moisture trends is the citing review's own extrapolation; the study only supplies the conceptual principle (maximise production per unit water, protect sensitive stages). Technology mismatch: deficit irrigation regimes, not app scheduling.

notes: Full text appears complete. Mostly a narrative review with a small amount of original experimental data (peach experiment near Cordoba, 2005 season) and model fits to prior Cordoba sunflower experiments; no work on digital scheduling tools.
